description: Making one voice sit next to another in a documentary or podcast mix: long-term average spectrum (LTAS) EQ matching with opendubstage ltasmatch, bridging a TTS or cloned voice into a location recording (band-limit, early reflections, room-tone floor), riding and placing an off-mic second speaker, phone and tape-sync matching, and when two voices should deliberately stay different. Use when a narrator and a pickup line sound like different rooms, when synthetic or re-recorded lines must blend with original tape, when an interviewer's interjections are buried, when a phone caller sits against a studio voice, or when someone asks for "EQ match", "dialogue match", "make these voices match" or "the bridge sounds dry and clinical". Do NOT use for cleaning a single recording (dialogue-editing-and-restoration) or for voice cloning itself.
